blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Use any smartphone, tablet or wearable that works for your project' — device-agnostic, consumer-app deployment model
blind_spots.operator_reality: GFE-approved hardware only, no app-store OTA updates, and no assumption of continuous connectivity to push app/content updates in a DDIL AF network environment
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the app was built for commercial industrial workforce training (Schneider Electric partnership) and ported to a single AF squadron pilot without re-architecting for military network constraints
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Use any smartphone, tablet or wearable that works for your project.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Mission-planning/debrief MR tool for the 349th ARS is described purely as 'software application licenses'
blind_spots.operator_reality: Licenses don't get you onto an Air Force network — an ATO/RMF package, STIGs, and IL4/IL5 accreditation are the actual gate between demo and fielded use, and there's no sign that work has started
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the SBIR abstract is framed around integrating XR into 'current mission planning and mission d[ebrief]' workflow, not around the compliance path to get there
blind_spots.evidence_quote: XR Solutions, Inc. will provide adapted user interfaces and the corresponding software application licenses for the 349th Air Refueling Squadron.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A mission-planning/situational tool for Air Force operators never mentions ATAK/TAK integration
blind_spots.operator_reality: AF and joint programs increasingly expect situational-awareness tools to plug into the TAK ecosystem rather than stand alone; building a bespoke MR app outside that ecosystem risks becoming a one-squadron pilot that never generalizes to a program of record
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: the product architecture appears to be a proprietary commercial MR app repurposed for one squadron rather than designed for the AF SA tooling ecosystem
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This will accelerate DAF requirements to integrate XR technology into current mission planning and mission d[ebrief]

opener_hook: Your 2022 Air Force Phase II SBIR ($749,985) built a mixed-reality mission-planning app for the 349th Air Refueling Squadron — four years on, the team is still sized at 4-5 with no public sign of a Phase III transition.
what_they_do: Mixed/augmented reality workforce app (Future Sight AR) with a commercial industrial partnership (Schneider Electric) and a 2022 Air Force Phase II SBIR for mission-planning/debrief with the 349th Air Refueling Squadron.
